basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 12.' and it opens '(Vers. 12 et 13.) Et peperit Zelpha ancilla Liae filium secundum Jacob: et dixit Lia,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 12 et 13.) Et peperit Zelpha ancilla Liae filium secundum Jacob: et dixit Lia, Beata ego, quia beatificant me mulieres: et vocavit nomen ejus Aser, divitiae. Male additae sunt divitiae, id est, πλοῦτος [Al. πλουτῶν], cum etymologia nominis Aser Scripturae auctoritate pandatur dicentis: Beata sum ego, et beatificant me mulieres. Et ab eo quod beata dicatur ab hominibus [Al. omnibus], filium suum beatum vocaverit; ASER (אשר) ergo non divitiae, sed beatus dicitur, dumtaxat in praesenti loco. Nam in aliis secundum ambiguitatem verbi possunt et divitiae sic vocari.
